title: Derived pullback without flatness
as_he_states: Whether Lf* and its tensor/Hom identities still work when f is not flat; scan106 retracts the naive injective argument.
plausible_today: Derived inverse image exists for morphisms of ringed topoi and is composition-compatible and monoidal. Use K-flat/K-injective or the appropriate bounded resolutions.
state_of_art: Stacks21.18 (tag06YV) supplies this formulation. The elementary f_* injective-preservation proof needs exact f*.
why_open: The pages themselves identify the flaw. No historical cause beyond that correction is documented.
worth: Useful as a short commentary task explaining the correction, not as an unsolved theorem.

title: Finite relative cohomological dimension over a noetherian base
as_he_states: “C’est peut-être vrai dès que Y est noethérien”: remove the finite-type-over-a-field restriction.
plausible_today: For finite-type f over a finite-dimensional noetherian base and an invertible prime ell, relative ell-cohomological dimension is finite. The unrestricted noetherian/coefficient version must be kept separate.
state_of_art: Gabber–Illusie XVIII_A Cor1.4 proves the stated finite-dimensional prime-to-characteristic case; Stacks59.96.2 covers finite-type schemes over a field.
why_open: The manuscript leaves a hope; the checked sources do not state why this exact broad wording was dropped.
worth: A bounded hypothesis comparison is worthwhile; the search does not justify advertising a new general theorem.

title: Projection coherence and resolution independence
as_he_states: “Il faut vérifier” functoriality and compatibilities of the constructed projection and Künneth maps.
plausible_today: For compactifiable morphisms and torsion coefficient sheaves in the stated bounded ranges, the canonical projection and external-product isomorphisms are natural and compatible with the six operations.
state_of_art: SGA4XVII5.2.9 and5.4.3 are exact statement matches;5.4.3.2 and5.4.3.5 leave auxiliary compatibility checks to the reader. This run does not claim a full re-proof of those diagrams.
why_open: The draft explicitly isolates coherence as the remaining task; Illusie later records how substantial compatibility work affected the trace formula.
worth: Worth a focused reconstruction of one named diagram, with the original models and signs fixed.

title: Ordinary Künneth without properness
as_he_states: He expects ordinary Künneth when n is prime to the characteristic, even if neither factor is proper.
plausible_today: For finite-type schemes over a separably closed field and invertible n, the derived Z/n Künneth formula holds.
state_of_art: Stacks59.97.9 proves exactly this. The unrestricted p-primary version is false, with the Artin–Schreier xy counterexample in C-SA13-017.
why_open: The page distinguishes the obstacle from the proper case; it gives no later abandonment history. The conditional Verdier priority remark remains historical evidence only.
worth: The mathematical question is settled; a concise historical comparison would improve the companion.

title: Curve Lefschetz formula with nonconstant coefficients
as_he_states: Prove the curve case with nonconstant coefficients and correct local terms, as a route to rationality.
plausible_today: Use constructible prime-to-characteristic ell-adic coefficients and the exact local terms of a cohomological correspondence; stalk traces need extra hypotheses.
state_of_art: Bourbaki279 §§5–6 announces the reduction; SGA5III,III B,XII contain the completed formulations. Illusie distinguishes the independent curve route from the later general compatibility proof.
why_open: Illusie documents missing compatibility arguments and the1974–1975 work; this does not prove a personal motive or a date for these sheets.
worth: A precise page-to-publication concordance is valuable, but re-solving the established trace theorem is unnecessary.

title: Passage from finite-level traces to ell-adic coefficients
as_he_states: Compatibility in n, projective limits, and extraction of the ell-adic trace needed for functions L.
plausible_today: Compatible perfect finite-level systems admit compatible traces; the full adic six-operation theory requires its finiteness and derived-limit hypotheses.
state_of_art: SGA5V–VI andXIV=XV provide the published setting. The independently checked certificate covers finite-projective Z_ell models and their reductions, not all derived limits.
why_open: SGA5 introduction explicitly notes that its V–VI do not build a full derived category of ell-adic sheaves. No reason for this sheet’s unfinished paragraph is stated.
worth: Worth isolating the exact adic hypothesis in a commentary task, avoiding a claim that the elementary calculation solves the whole formalism.

title: Definition and independence of perfect-complex trace
as_he_states: Show the alternating trace descends through resolutions and has the expected additivity, duality and tensor properties.
plausible_today: A perfect object has a canonical categorical trace. Strictly compatible cone diagrams have additive trace; arbitrary endomorphisms of abstract triangles need not.
state_of_art: Stacks64.10.2 and21.48 give the positive statements;110.65 gives the counterexample. The sheet132→134 supplies the later resolution argument itself.
why_open: The same-text development resolves much of the initial question. Illusie reports Ferrand’s1968 counterexample to the stronger abstract assertion.
worth: Worth making the distinction explicit because the earlier notes blurred the two additivity claims.

title: Global Tor dimension after compact-support cohomology
as_he_states: The question begun at136 is developed into the uniform Tor bounds and Rf! estimate at138–142.
plausible_today: For compactifiable finite-type f with fibers of dimension≤d and the draft’s uniform Tor interval [N,M], the homological interval becomes [N−2d,M]; constructibility and noetherian coefficient hypotheses supply perfectness over a point.
state_of_art: SGA4XVII5.2.10,5.3.6–8 give the corresponding finiteness statements. The sign conversion and uniformity requirement are independently checked.
why_open: This is largely an open step answered later in the same supplied text, not evidence of a surviving conjecture.
worth: Useful for one worked example and a warning about nonuniform stalk bounds; no new general research claim follows.

title: Construction of the local trace pairing
as_he_states: The correspondence pairing is started on144, partly deleted, and rebuilt on146 using duality and Koszul signs; boundedness is struck in one passage.
plausible_today: Dualizable/perfect coefficient objects admit evaluation-defined local pairings with H⁰ in the correct place. Finite Tor amplitude alone is insufficient; an unbounded model must not be traced term by term.
state_of_art: SGA5III/III B supply the published framework. Lu–Zheng2022 Th2.16 and2.21 give a relative dualizability criterion and a proper-pushforward pairing formula under explicit noetherian, torsion, finite-Tor and local-acyclicity hypotheses.
why_open: The visible cancellation is a revision, not evidence of rejection of local trace. Illusie’s chronology records later compatibility work; the scan is needed for the deleted word.
worth: High-value companion work: reconstruct the single typed pairing with the two shifts and evaluation map fixed.

title: Broader ordinary projection formula
as_he_states: The paragraph about locally constant finite-type cohomology and a qcqs relaxation is left with an unfinished “où”.
plausible_today: Perfect target complexes satisfy projection on arbitrary ringed topoi. For constant noetherian coefficient rings and finite relative cd, bounded-above finite-free resolutions permit the stated way-out extension; qcqs alone is not a replacement for all colimit hypotheses.
state_of_art: Stacks21.50.1 and SGA4XVII5.2.11–12 are the checked positive formulations. The exact maximal range of the unfinished sentence was not identified.
why_open: The text is unfinished; the sources opened do not explain why it was left so.
worth: Worth a small hypothesis audit, with no claim that the familiar perfect case is open.
